interim_updates.note_text: Ceylon Hotels Corporation PLC (CHOT) reported Group Revenue of Rs.438,035k for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), +25.1% YoY (2025: Rs.350,122k), and Group Gross Profit of Rs.318,190k, +33.8% YoY (2025: Rs.237,787k) -- genuine operational improvement, with the operating loss narrowing 36.5% to Rs.(48,972)k (2025: Rs.(77,197)k). However, the Group's bottom line moved the other way: Profit/(loss) for the period widened to a Rs.(70,652)k loss from a Rs.(50,620)k loss YoY (+39.6% larger loss), because two below-the-operating-line items swung sharply negative. First, Share of loss of equity-accounted investees (the Group's joint ventures -- Ceylon Holidays Holding, CHC Rest House, and Suisse Hotel Kandy, per Note 1; the filing does not disclose which specific JV(s) drove the swing) widened 881% YoY to Rs.(53,252)k from Rs.(5,429)k, a Rs.47,823k deterioration -- the single largest driver of the wider Group loss. Second, Income tax swung from a Rs.31,217k reversal/credit in Q1 FY2025/26 to a Rs.(16,447)k expense this quarter, a Rs.47,664k negative swing, also unexplained in the filing. These two negative swings (combined Rs.95,487k) were substantially offset by a Rs.47,229k improvement in Net finance income to Rs.48,019k from just Rs.790k YoY, itself driven by a Net foreign exchange gain of Rs.40,956k versus Rs.9,333k PY (+339%, a Rs.31,623k favourable swing) plus Finance income +40.8% to Rs.70,272k (2025: Rs.49,916k). Selling and distribution expenses rose 117.2% YoY to Rs.50,550k (2025: Rs.23,269k), a large increase not explained by any note (possibly a marketing or occupancy-driving push, but not stated); Administration expenses rose a more modest 8.2% to Rs.317,886k. No occupancy rate, average room rate, or tourism-season commentary is disclosed anywhere in this filing -- Note 3 explicitly states 'there are no distinguishable components to be identified as segments for the company', so results are also not broken out by hotel property (Galle Face Hotel and the Group's other properties under United Hotels Company, Kandy Hotels Company (1938), Suisse Hotels, etc. are not individually shown). At the Company (standalone parent, a holding entity with no direct hotel revenue) level, results moved favourably: PBT +77.1% YoY to Rs.15,575k (2025: Rs.8,794k) and PAT +31.5% to Rs.14,992k (2025: Rs.11,402k), driven by Finance income (interest on loans to subsidiaries/JVs) rising 49.2% to Rs.17,383k (2025: Rs.11,649k).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is CHOT's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (no closer prior quarter previously stored; the most recent prior manual document registered for CHOT, source_id manual_91e691cdf4cd9be9, covered the quarter ended 30 Sep 2025 and was superseded by this fresher quarter-ended-30-June-2026 filing, source_id 52676). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) no occupancy rate, average room rate, or per-property revenue breakdown is disclosed anywhere -- Note 3 explicitly states there are no distinguishable segments, which is a notable gap for a hospitality group with multiple hotel properties (Galle Face Hotel and Group subsidiaries United Hotels, Kandy Hotels Company (1938), Suisse Hotels, Ceylon Hotels Maldives) and no tourism-season commentary either; (2) the Rs.47,823k YoY widening in Share of loss of equity-accounted investees is not explained, and the filing does not disclose which of the three JVs (Ceylon Holidays Holding, CHC Rest House, Suisse Hotel Kandy) drove it; (3) the 117.2% YoY jump in Selling and distribution expenses (Rs.23,269k to Rs.50,550k) is not explained by any note; (4) the c.47.7mn swing in tax from a credit to an expense is not explained; (5) an internal inconsistency was found within the filing itself: the Statement of Financial Position's split of Total Equity between owners (Rs.8,161,218k) and non-controlling interest (Rs.2,930,222k) at 30 June 2026 does not match the Statement of Changes in Equity's closing split for the same date (Rs.8,083,606k owners / Rs.3,007,835k NCI) -- Total Equity itself is identical and correct in both (Rs.11,091,441k), so this appears to be a presentational allocation inconsistency in CHOT's own filing, not a transcription error in this DB, and does not affect any figure used here; (6) this PDF's text layer uses a Type3 font with no ToUnicode CMap and could not be extracted by any text-layer tool -- all figures were read visually off 220dpi page renders (documented in financial_statements.notes).
interim_updates.takeaway: CHOT's headline Q1 FY2026/27 result -- a wider Group net loss of Rs.(70,652)k versus Rs.(50,620)k a year earlier -- looks worse than the underlying hotel business actually performed: Revenue grew 25.1%, Gross Profit grew 33.8%, and the operating loss narrowed 36.5%. The wider bottom-line loss is entirely a below-the-operating-line story, split between a Rs.47,823k larger loss from the Group's equity-accounted joint ventures and a Rs.47,664k adverse tax swing, both unexplained in the filing and both largely offset (but not fully) by a Rs.47,229k FX-driven improvement in net finance income. None of occupancy, ADR, or per-property performance is disclosed, which limits how much can be said about the underlying operational drivers of the strong Revenue and Gross Profit growth.

operational_highlights: Group Revenue Rs.438,035k, +25.1% YoY (2025: Rs.350,122k); Gross Profit Rs.318,190k, +33.8% YoY; operating loss narrowed 36.5% to Rs.(48,972)k (2025: Rs.(77,197)k) -- genuine operating improvement.
Despite the operating improvement, Group Profit/(loss) for the period WIDENED to Rs.(70,652)k from Rs.(50,620)k YoY (+39.6% larger loss), driven entirely by items below the operating line.

Share of loss of equity-accounted joint ventures widened 881% YoY to Rs.(53,252)k (2025: Rs.(5,429)k, a Rs.47,823k deterioration) -- the single largest driver of the wider Group loss; the filing does not disclose which JV(s) drove it.
Income tax swung from a Rs.31,217k credit/reversal PY to a Rs.(16,447)k expense this quarter (a Rs.47,664k negative swing), unexplained in the filing.
Net finance income improved Rs.47,229k YoY to Rs.48,019k, driven by a Rs.31,623k favourable swing in net FX gain (Rs.40,956k vs Rs.9,333k PY) -- nearly offsetting the JV-loss and tax swings.
No occupancy, ADR, or per-property segment disclosure anywhere in the filing (Note 3: 'no distinguishable components to be identified as segments').
Company (holding-entity) level: PBT +77.1% YoY to Rs.15,575k, PAT +31.5% to Rs.14,992k, driven by intercompany Finance income +49.2% to Rs.17,383k.
key_drivers: Share of loss of equity-accounted joint ventures widened Rs.47,823k YoY (881%, to Rs.(53,252)k) -- the dominant driver of the wider Group net loss, though the specific underperforming JV is not identified in the filing.
A Rs.47,664k negative swing in income tax (from a Rs.31,217k credit to a Rs.16,447k expense) compounded the JV-loss drag, unexplained in the filing.

These were substantially offset by a Rs.47,229k improvement in net finance income, itself driven by a Rs.31,623k favourable FX swing plus 40.8% higher finance income -- without this offset the Group loss would have widened far more sharply.

Core hotel operations improved genuinely: Gross Profit +33.8% YoY and the operating loss narrowed 36.5%, showing the underlying hospitality business trended favourably even though the headline PAT trend (a wider loss) suggests otherwise.
